audit.report: A batch_replayable_inventory workload (inventory_reconcile, pid 1010499) idled in transaction for 4.2s, blocking checkout sessions and collapsing checkout success to 0% (120/120 failed over 30s) with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed termination; the Continuity Guardian accepted because waiting ~896s would cost ~$274,712 and exceed the 60s degradation tolerance. The first contract was denied when the blocker restarted (new pid 1010979), triggering a rapid renegotiation that also concluded in one round. Termination executed and verification confirmed recovery: zero lock waits, checkout 100% success (36/36 over 10s), no protected settlements aborted.
audit.root_cause: The inventory_reconcile batch job held an idle-in-transaction lock (SELECT 1) that blocked all checkout sessions, driving checkout success to 0% and exceeding the 60s business tolerance.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile), enforce idle_in_transaction_session_timeout or statement_timeout to prevent idle transactions from blocking critical checkout paths.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians reasoned correctly and efficiently: the Database Guardian cited live evidence (idle blocker, checkout collapse, replayable workload) and the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection in one round each; the only delay was the authority's live_identity check correctly rejecting the stale pid after the blocker restarted.
follow_ups: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_worker role to auto-terminate idle transactions after 10s.
Create a pre-approved termination playbook for inventory_reconcile when it blocks checkout >30s, referencing its replayable/idempotent properties and 4-min replay cost.
Instrument monitoring to correlate batch_worker idle-in-transaction states with checkout latency spikes in real time.
